title: Ethiopian Hibiscus Tea
community: All of Ethiopia — the ruby-red herbal drink
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Hibiscus Tea — dried hibiscus flowers (roselle) steeped in hot water until deeply ruby red, sweetened with honey and served hot or cold with lemon. One of Africa's most beautiful herbal drinks — Ethiopia grows hibiscus (roselle) in its western regions.
longDesc: Ethiopian hibiscus tea (made from Hibiscus sabdariffa, also called roselle) produces a deeply red, tart, antioxidant-rich drink that is both beautiful and medicinal. Grown in western Ethiopia, it is increasingly popular across the country.
steps: Pour hot water over hibiscus flowers.
Steep 5—8 minutes until deeply ruby red.
Strain. Add honey and lemon juice.
Serve hot, or cool and serve over ice.
chefTips: The colour deepens the longer it steeps — 8 minutes for maximum colour and flavour.
cookingScience: Hibiscus anthocyanins are pH-sensitive — in acidic conditions (lemon juice) they turn brighter red; in alkaline conditions they turn blue-purple. The addition of lemon juice not only flavours the drink but maintains the vivid ruby colour.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian roselle from western regions — increasingly farmed as a cash crop for export.
servedWith: At celebrations as a colourful non-alcoholic drink
healthBenefits: Studies show hibiscus lowers blood pressure.
culturalNote: Ethiopian hibiscus tea is the ruby drink of western Ethiopia — beautiful to look at, tart to drink, and full of the most powerful antioxidants available in any tea. It is both medicine and ceremony.
